clue.text: Supply disreputable bar patron's first strong drink

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, so the letters move flexibly into a new order
bar here means except, so one letter is left out of the word before it
first asks for only the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of patron, the one to remove

explanation.surface: A shady pub regular is supplied with a stiff first drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb but is the adverb from supple; DISREPUTABLE without its P rearranges to BUILDERS TEA. Builder's tea is British slang for strong, sweet tea in a mug.
explanation.definitionFit: Builder's tea is the British name for very strong brewed tea, the kind tradesmen drink, so it is a strong drink.

clue.text: Bird unexpectedly blown around Arkansas

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly is out of its usual order, so the letters are rearranged
around means the reworked letters sit on either side of the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: the letters of blown rearranged
AR is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Arkansas

explanation.surface: A bird is blown off course over the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown' passes for the bird's plight in a gale, but it is the fodder; the state abbreviation sits inside after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The barn owl is a pale owl species that nests in farm buildings, so it is a bird.

clue.text: Enter, wearing throw

blocks.note: dressed in something is wearing it
to put the shot is to throw it

explanation.surface: Someone comes in while wearing a throw, a blanket over the shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data into a computer is to input it, a verb sense the two words share.

clue.text: Very plain, oddly impassive

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in the first, third and fifth places of the word before it

blocks.note: dead as an intensifier, as in dead easy
the odd-numbered letters of plain

explanation.surface: Something is very plain and strangely expressionless.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face or delivery shows no emotion, which is what impassive describes.

clue.text: Note inspector's feeling of guilt

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
Inspector Morse, the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the TV series

explanation.surface: A detective's note records a feeling of guilt, as if a suspect confessed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of inspector's means 'is' joining the parts, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for a wrong done, a synonym for the feeling of guilt.

clue.text: International accord bears examination

blocks.note: a test is an examination
to accord is to agree or match

explanation.surface: An international agreement is put under scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'bears' puts the second part beneath the first: the accord holds up the examination. A Test match is an international cricket or rugby game.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is a full international fixture between national sides, so 'International' is the noun used for it.

clue.text: Little Scottish boy endlessly absorbed by an Arabic folk tale

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off
something absorbed by another thing is taken inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
laddie is the Scots word for a young lad

explanation.surface: A small Scots boy is engrossed in an Arabian Nights story.
explanation.walkthrough: LADDIE loses its final E and sits between the A and N of an.
explanation.definitionFit: Aladdin is a story usually grouped with the Arabian Nights tales, an Arabic folk tale.

clue.text: Battery packs hold power, in general

indicators.note: a battery that packs something holds it inside

blocks.note: AA is a standard battery size
a hold is a grip
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Battery packs retain their power in general use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battery packs' reads as a noun phrase, but 'packs' is the verb doing the containing. 'In general' looks like a stock phrase; the general is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was the Roman commander who won Actium for Augustus, a famous general.

clue.text: Hurriedly leave after a new fellow enters sailor's joint

indicators.note: what enters goes inside the word that follows it

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, with the 's
taken as written
N is the usual abbreviation for new
a don is a college fellow
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Someone bolts after a newcomer barges into a seaman's pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts as a bar or dive; it is the body's hip. The 's of sailor's supplies a letter, split around the inserted fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandon ship is the order to get off a sinking vessel at once, so figuratively to leave in a hurry.

clue.text: Setter's returned prize in error

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the short word is read from right to left

blocks.note: the setter is 'I', so setter's is I'M
the stake is the prize money at stake in a contest

explanation.surface: A setter admits giving back a prize awarded by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is an error, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Yoga clothes livened up part of Bible study

indicators.note: livening something up shakes it about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, eleven letters

explanation.surface: Exercise wear brightens up a Bible class.
explanation.definitionFit: Eschatology is the branch of theology about the end times, the Last Judgement and Revelation, studied as part of Bible scholarship.

clue.text: Close to old border guards

indicators.note: guards means surrounds and protects, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: to abut is to border on
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Near an ancient frontier patrolled by guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old border' looks like one thing; 'border' is the verb ABUT wrapped around 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: About can mean near or approximately, as in 'about here', so it fits close to.

clue.text: NHS worker and assistant knocked back drink, taking a minute

indicators.note: knocked back means turned the other way, so the drink is read in reverse
taking means accepting something inside it

blocks.note: PA is a personal assistant
cider is an apple drink
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A health worker and an aide down a quick drink, taking a minute off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' sounds like drinking; it turns CIDER round. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramedic crews an ambulance for the National Health Service, so is an NHS worker.

clue.text: Swimmer's husband, on record, admitted to murder

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside, so these letters go into the next word

blocks.note: to do in is to murder
an LP is a long-playing record
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A swimmer's husband, on the record, confessed to murder.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, 'on' puts the husband after the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a marine mammal, so a swimmer is a cryptic way to describe it.

clue.text: Each detective on time to visit Polish memorial

indicators.note: to visit is to go into a place, so these letters go inside the next word

blocks.note: to hone is to sharpen or polish
ea is the abbreviation for each
DS is a detective sergeant
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Each detective spends time visiting a Polish war memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P suggests Poland; it is the verb polish.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone is the stone marking a grave, a memorial to the dead.

clue.text: Parisian is on island, close to Mafia country

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

blocks.note: est is French for is
taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island
the last letter of Mafia

explanation.surface: A Parisian is on a Mediterranean island near Mafia country, Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic state, a country in northern Europe.

clue.text: Condescension or mansplaining is rather too much for some French folk

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters are a run taken from inside the words before

blocks.note: the run straddles the end of the first word, all of or, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Some French people find patronising behaviour and men explaining things a bit much.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans are the people of Normandy in northern France, so they are some French folk.

clue.text: Spooner's achieved more money for landing sites

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of two words

blocks.note: achieved is won and more money is a raise; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having secured a pay increase for airport facilities.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the W and R sounds of WON RAISE gives RUN WAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Runways are the strips aircraft touch down on, the landing sites of an airfield.

clue.text: Sign my Private Eye covers for this reason? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: covers means wraps round, so one piece goes around another
this flips the stated relation, so the cover and the covered swap roles

blocks.note: so means therefore, for this reason
cor! is a British exclamation like my!
a PI is a private investigator, a private eye

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the satirical magazine Private Eye runs horoscopes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, my private eye would wrap the reason; 'Quite the opposite' reverses that, so the reason wraps the rest. Private Eye is a British satirical magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, the scorpion.

clue.text: Cross after graphic artist fails to start animated piece

indicators.note: failing to start means the first letter is lost
after sends the piece named before it to the second position, behind the artist

blocks.note: M. C. Escher, the Dutch graphic artist of impossible staircases
a zo or dzo is a cross between a yak and a domestic cow

explanation.surface: An angry person follows a cartoonist who cannot get going on an animated film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is a hybrid animal. 'After' puts that piece after the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively, playful movement in a symphony or sonata, so an animated piece of music.

clue.text: Chairman of the Board of Trustees in a tracksuit

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words around it

blocks.note: the run starts at the last letter of the first word and ends inside the last

explanation.surface: The head of a board of trustees turns up in a tracksuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chairman of the Board' reads as a company title; it is Frank Sinatra's nickname. The hiding 'in' also sits inside the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was nicknamed the Chairman of the Board for his dominance of popular singing.

clue.text: Agent fabricates things in answers

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent
to fabricate things is to tell untruths

explanation.surface: A spy makes things up when answering questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Replies are answers, as nouns or as verbs, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Announces Labour Party success, ousting independent

indicators.note: ousting means throwing out, so one letter is removed from the word before

blocks.note: hands are workers, labour
a do is a party
a win is a success
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A Labour Party victory is announced after an independent is unseated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour Party' reads as the British political party; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge hands down a ruling when delivering it formally, so hands down means announces.

clue.text: Animal in river

blocks.note: something in is fashionable, hip
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: An animal wallows in a river, just as a hippo would.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a cryptic definition of a river-dweller, but 'in' means fashionable and the river is the Po.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippo is the short form of hippopotamus, a large African animal.

clue.text: Very excited shrill noise cat makes when escaping from trap

indicators.note: trap is slang for mouth, and what escapes from the mouth is heard spoken

blocks.note: a shrill noise is high-pitched
a contented cat purrs

explanation.surface: A cat shrieks with excitement as it gets free of a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' looks like a snare the cat escapes; it is slang for the mouth, so the sounds HIGH and PURR are spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyper is informal for overexcited and full of nervous energy.

clue.text: Guardiola accepts a little bit of money for food

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the following letters go inside the name

blocks.note: Pep Guardiola, the football manager
taken as written
a sou was a French coin of small value

explanation.surface: The football manager takes a small payment to spend on meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea soup is a thick soup of dried peas, so a kind of food.

clue.text: Somewhat drunkenly upset heartless fool

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word is taken out

blocks.note: to tip over is to upset
a silly is a foolish person

explanation.surface: A cruel idiot gets annoyed while fairly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsy means slightly drunk, so acting tipsily is behaving somewhat drunkenly.

clue.text: Dinosaur outrages us, rudely grabbing waitress's rear

indicators.note: rudely suggests rough treatment, so the letters are knocked into a new order
the rear of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of waitress

explanation.surface: A prehistoric beast scandalises diners by grabbing a waitress's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grabbing' adds the S to the letters before the reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The stegosaurus is a plated, spike-tailed Jurassic dinosaur.
